as_told.title: ScanPyramids muon scanning funded by a Japanese team with the Ministry of Antiquities

plain: Since 2015 a research effort called the ScanPyramids project has been looking for hidden empty spaces inside the pyramids at Giza in Egypt. It does this by using muons, tiny particles that rain down on Earth from space and pass through stone. The researcher Filippo Biondi, who has scanned beneath the pyramids himself by other means, describes it in a December 2025 episode. He says ScanPyramids "is using muons which are sub particles that are emitted from the universe." By measuring how many of these particles get through the stone, the team can spot hollow areas. The researcher Jeffrey Drum tells more about the project in a 2026 episode and cites the team's published paper on its muon work. Drum says the scientists work with "a Japanese team that's been sponsoring and providing the funding for all of this", together with Egypt's Ministry of Antiquities, the government office that oversees ancient sites. The project is brought up because it shows that the pyramids may still hold rooms nobody has entered.
